transaction_contract.exact_id_conflict: ON CONFLICT (stripe_event_id) DO NOTHING RETURNING id — zero rows means exact stripe_event_id already claimed; ROLLBACK + HTTP 200 idempotent reason=stripe_event_id_already_claimed; no_db_write=true (no durable write from this request)
transaction_contract.addon_no_pre_transaction_already_paid_sh: Matched addon_service events never early-return on stale lookup already-paid; always BEGIN → claim → FOR UPDATE reload → exact-id or under-lock distinct-business → mark processed → COMMIT
transaction_contract.addon_distinct_event_already_paid: After claim + FOR UPDATE reload, if payment already paid: do not rewrite payment/service; mark claimed event processed with privacy-safe duplicate_business_outcome; COMMIT; HTTP 200 idempotent reason=duplicate_business_outcome; no_business_mutation=true + no_payment_or_service_rewrite=true (never no_db_write — ledger claim is a DB write)
transaction_contract.addon_ineligible_under_lock: If lock miss or payment_kind != addon_service → fail closed ROLLBACK + retryable 500
transaction_contract.pre_commit_failure: ROLLBACK claim+mutations + HTTP 500 retryable (mutation/processed/claim failures before commit attempt)
transaction_contract.commit_failure: AMBIGUOUS — never claim rejected COMMIT definitely rolled back. Best-effort ROLLBACK then HTTP 500 retryable outcome_unknown=true (no secret/error details). Retry resolves via durable stripe_event_id claim if commit landed, or can claim if it did not.
transaction_contract.payload: allowlisted non-PII identifiers/state only; never raw Stripe event/session/customer/email/phone/name/addresses/tokens; duplicate_business_outcome marker allowed

compatibility.distinct_event_business_idempotency: preserved (addon: FOR UPDATE lock/reload; booking: existing under-lock already_paid)
